newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton ranged on low arrivals, poor demand.
newsitem.headline: India cotton ranged on low arrivals, poor demand.

text.p: Cotton prices held steady amid limited demand from millers coupled with low arrivals on Wednesday, dealers said.
"Markets in Gujarat region were closed today due to suspension of work called by political parties which in turn affected inflow of cotton from Gujarat to local markets," one broker said.
In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan was quiet at 14,000/14,300 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) as was Wagad cotton at 12,700/12,800 rupees per candy.
Bengal-deshi was steady at 945/1,000 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) as was Punjab saw-ginned at 1,800/1,840 rupees and F-414 at 2,050/2,070 rupees per maund.

Traders put unsold stock at the end of the current cotton season at 2.40/2.50 million bales (170 kg each), largely with state-owned agencies and cotton traders though some millers have enough stock for two or three months' production.
